title: Sans-serif, monospaced, and roman fonts versus serif and italic for dyslexia
statement:
For readers with dyslexia, sans-serif, monospaced, and roman fonts (such as Helvetica, Courier, and Arial) significantly outperform serif and italic fonts in reading speed and objective legibility.

Options:
- Optimal Sans-Serifs: Helvetica / Arial (fits: universal design, corporate communication)
- Wide Sans-Serif: Verdana (fits: accessibility first, educational platforms)
- Optimal Monospace: Courier (fits: code blocks, specialized dyslexia modes)
- No Slanted Text: Avoid Italics (fits: all accessible designs)
appliesWhen: Applies to: web, edtech, reading apps. Audience: children under 10, adults, general.

source.title: Good Fonts for Dyslexia
source.venue: Proceedings of the 15th International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility (ASSETS '13)
